newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-AGASSI STRUGGLES BUT WINS ON RETURN IN SAN JOSE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AGASSI STRUGGLES BUT WINS ON RETURN IN SAN JOSE.

text.p: In his first match on the tour since being booed out of the ATP Championships in November, Andre Agassi had to struggle mightily Wednesday to get past Bahamian Davis Cupper Mark Knowles 6-4 4-6 6-2 in the first round of the $303,000 Sybase Open.

"I expected to be more rusty than I was," the third-seeded Agassi said. "I don't expect my game to come back quickly, it's just nice to be playing again. At this stage, I'm just looking to improve match by match. I'm in it for the long haul."
World number one Pete Sampras advanced to the quarter-finals, beating up-and-coming American Justin Gimelstob 6-2 6-3 in a second-round match.
"It was like playing Super Nintendo," Gimelstob said. "He'll go down as the best ever. Hopefully for the rest of us, he won't be around too much longer."

With his vaunted return of serve and his trademark powerful groundstrokes off-kilter, the 12th-ranked Agassi had to fight tooth and nail for nearly every point as the net-rushing Knowles refused to give up the centre of the court.
"I'm a grinder out there," said Agassi, who registered his first tour win since October 24. "As the match wears on, I'll break a person down and cause a few errors."
Knowles, who roomed with Agassi for four years at the Nick Bollettieri Academy when they were juniors, said his opponent appears to have regained his mental edge.
"I was impressed, " Knowles said. "He looked fresh and eager to get back. Any time he sets his mind to it, he's beautiful to watch. He's definitely one of the most talented players out there."
Agassi said he plans to return to glory in 1997, after finishing 1996 without a Grand Slam title and failing to reach a final of any of the four majors.

"With my kind of game, it's not easy to sustain myself at 100 percent for 12 months," Agassi said. "My game is more difficult to sustain than either Pete's (Sampras) or Goran's (Ivanisevic) because they can get a lot of easy points off their serves.
"I need a certain intensity. But I've been able to do it for a year at a time in the past and I can do it again."

In other action involving seeded players on Wednesday, eighth seed Chris Woodruff of the United States beat France's Jean Philippe Fleurian 6-2 6-3 and American Richey Reneberg, the sixth seed, beat Canada's Sebastien Lareau 6-3 5-7 6-4.
